Cigarette butts are the most common trash collected across Metro Manila, and that fact should stop anyone in their tracks. They top the list because they are routinely tossed onto streets, sidewalks, and drainage grates, often within sight of a trash bin. This is a habit, a casual and repeated act by smokers who treat public spaces as personal ashtrays and the streets as a garbage can.

Based on the latest 2025 littering apprehension data from the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority, cigarette butts lead by a wide margin. Candy wrappers come next, followed by plastic waste. The remaining top items include paper trash such as tissues, receipts, bus tickets, and face masks, as well as obstructions left on sidewalks and roads. Together, they form the city’s everyday pollution footprint.

The consequences show up most clearly in business and commercial areas, where littered streets clog drainage, worsen flooding, and push up cleaning and maintenance costs. Dirtier sidewalks discourage foot traffic, affect how districts are perceived, and quietly undermine the everyday activity that small businesses rely on. Over time, these pressures translate into higher operating expenses and greater strain on public resources, costs that are ultimately absorbed by residents and enterprises alike.

MMDA continues to remind the public to follow proper waste disposal rules, but the numbers point to a deeper issue of daily behavior rather than a lack of regulation.

What would you do if you saw someone flicking their cigarette butt onto the street?

Report by Kenneth M. del Rosario

#radarPHBusiness #radarPH

Nakipag-ugnayan sa Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) ang Department of Transportation (DoTr) para sa update ng isinasagawang South Commuter Rail Project at ilang plano sa ilalim nito.

Sa coordination meeting na pinangunahan ni MMDA General Manager USec. Nicolas D. Torre III, tinalakay ang planong pagtatayo ng istasyon sa East Service, San Martin De Porres, Paranaque City at panukalang drainage alignment sa bahagi ng Makati City.

Ilan sa kanilang napagkasunduan ang pagsasagawa ng site inspection, pagsusumite ng DOTr ng traffic management plan at pakikipag-ugnayan sa lokal na pamahalaan ng Parañaque at Makati City ukol sa proyekto.

Kasama rin sa pulong si MMDA TEC Director Engr. Francisco Pesino Jr. at MMDA Flood Control and Sewerage Management Director Mark Navarro.
#mmda
